title: Hanaoka Seishu operates for breast cancer under general anaesthesia
summary: On 13 October 1804 the Japanese surgeon Hanaoka Seishu operated on a 60-year-old woman, Kan Aiya, for breast cancer after giving her tsusensan, a herbal compound he had refined for almost 20 years. One review calls it the world's first successful breast cancer surgery under general anaesthesia, 38 years before C. W. Long's ether trial in 1842.

as_recorded.value: On October 13, 1804, Dr. Hanaoka performed a partial mastectomy on a 60-year-old woman

where.modern_name: Wakayama Prefecture, Japan (Hanaoka practised at Hirayama; its exact site is not confirmed on an opened page)

importance.justification: An early documented use of general anaesthesia for major surgery, decades before ether anaesthesia in the West.
